name: basque pepper stews
instructions:
The house for the basque/southern-european pepper stews — merged from southern chickpea soup + caraway tomato stew (2026-11-12). THE LINKING CORE: CHICKEN STOCK + RAW TOMATO + BELL PEPPERS. The variants are just all the things we can do with it.

'Southern' as in southern european — riviera to iberia; the chickpea variants sit apart from the indian curry side of the chickpea family ([[chana-masala]], [[himachali-chana-madra]]).

=== VARIANT A — CHICKPEA + CHARD (VERIFIED, THE ORIGINAL) ===

INGREDIENTS:
- chickpeas
- yellow onions (yellow only, I think — see notes)
- celery (experiment confirmed — onion/green pepper/celery base; see notes)
- garlic
- swiss chard — stalks AND leaves both good: sauté the STALKS in the soffrito, leaves in later (see notes)
- bay leaf
- CHICKEN STOCK (required — see the stock note)
- tomato — FRESH, necessary (canned is too saucy; see notes)
- tomato paste
- bell pepper
- olive oil
- oregano (works well here — see notes)
- old bay + lemon zest (primary seasonings — see notes)
- lemon juice (secondary — tried; see notes)
- salt and black pepper

No dairy, and no seasonings beyond the oregano + bay leaf.

=== VARIANT B — CARAWAY CHICKEN STEW (NEEDS WORK) ===

The meat build — same core, with shredded protein (chicken breast the tested default; pork and shrimp hypothesized — see notes), white wine, and caraway seeds. Anaheims preferred over bell here (funkier by design).

INGREDIENTS:
- SHREDDED CHICKEN BREAST (best here — not chicken thigh; see notes)
- ANAHEIM PEPPERS (preferred over green bell — maybe a little jalapeño too; see notes)
- tomato
- chicken stock
- yellow onion
- garlic
- carrot
- white wine
- CARAWAY SEEDS
- thyme
- sage
- olive oil
- salt and black pepper
- lemon juice (secondary — see notes)

PROCEDURE (SKETCH):

1. SOFRITO: sauté the onion, garlic, carrot, and anaheim (+ jalapeño if using), and cook the tomato down with them INTO A PASTE — this dish has sofrito discipline, not tomato-simmered-in-broth.
2. Deglaze with white wine; chicken stock in with the caraway seeds, thyme, and sage.
3. Poach and SHRED the chicken breast into it.
4. Lemon juice to taste at the end if it wants brightness.

=== VARIANT C — CHICKPEA + ESCAROLE (UNATTEMPTED) ===

The famous italian chickpea-and-escarole soup. Stock-based, chickpeas + escarole as the identity pair. To be filled in when cooked.

=== VARIANT D — INSTAPOT (BARLEY + BLACK/GREEN LENTILS) ===

The instapot version of the stew. Uses BARLEY and BLACK/GREEN LENTILS (DRIED) instead of chickpeas — chickpeas are tough to instapot right. Same core: chicken stock + raw tomato + bell peppers. In this build you could SWAP THE PEPPERS FOR CARROTS if you wanted to — the peppers are more tied to the chickpeas (see notes; this swap might turn into a separate recipe eventually).
notes:
=== SCOPE — THE CORE IS CHICKEN STOCK + RAW TOMATO + BELL PEPPERS ===

Merged 2026-11-12 from southern chickpea soup (variant A here, verified and good; plus the escarole plan, variant C) and caraway tomato stew (variant B here, still needs work). The linking thing is CHICKEN STOCK + RAW TOMATO + BELL PEPPERS — the variants are all the things we can do with it. The 'basque' name comes from the family rules first worked out in [[chicken-with-vinegar]] variant B: tomato + chicken stock + thyme.

=== THE BIGGEST NOTE — YOU NEED THE CHICKEN STOCK ===

Chicken stock is required. I experimented with splashes of vegetable, chicken, and beef broth before deciding CHICKEN BROTH is the right ingredient. Regular vegetable stock isn't flavorful enough on its own, and dark roasted / beef stock doesn't make sense as the base.

SPLASHES OF THE OTHER STOCKS FOR DEPTH: vegetable and beef broth are SECONDARY for exactly this purpose — a splash cut into the chicken base might add depth. This is deliberately a STOCK-FOCUSED family — that's what makes it different from a straight italian tomato soup with parmesan.

THE BALANCE: it should be MORE CHICKEN-STOCK-FLAVORED THAN TOMATO-FLAVORED overall — otherwise it turns into a SAUCE.

THE VEGETARIAN PATH — LIGHT/GARDEN VEGETABLE BOUILLON (WANT TO TRY): I could see all these versions using LIGHT VEGETABLE BOUILLON (GARDEN) instead of chicken to make it vegetarian. Note the tension with the rule above (plain vegetable stock wasn't flavorful enough in the original experiments) — the garden bouillon is the specific candidate, not generic veg stock. Untested.

=== RAW/FRESH TOMATO — PART OF THE CORE, NOT CANNED ===

Raw tomato is a third of the linking core. Same rule as [[minestrone-soup]] and the retired italian mushroomed lentils: FRESH tomato is necessary — canned doesn't work as good, too saucy. A BOX OF CHERRY TOMATOES is usually perfect — they're lighter. (In the caraway build the raw tomato gets cooked down into a paste in the sofrito — still fresh going in.)

=== THE PEPPER SLOT — BELL IS THE SPINE; ANAHEIM IN THE CARAWAY BUILD ===

BELL PEPPERS are the core's pepper. In the CARAWAY BUILD I think I prefer ANAHEIM PEPPERS (and maybe a little JALAPEÑO) — it's FUNKIER AND LESS SMOOTH BY DESIGN; green bell stays the fallback there and remains the pick in the smoother chickpea build.

=== HERBS — FAMILY-WIDE RULE: THYME + OREGANO YES, ROSEMARY NO ===

I think ALL of these variants like THYME and OREGANO and dislike ROSEMARY. Thyme is the basque spine herb ([[chicken-with-vinegar]] variant B), oregano is proven in the chickpea build, and rosemary is clashing across the whole family (consistent with its failures across the tomato + stock dishes — nothing here for it to grip).

=== CELERY — BUILD-DEPENDENT (SECONDARY) ===

- CHICKPEA BUILD (A): confirmed by experiment — the base is ONION / GREEN PEPPER / CELERY. Technically different from a soffrito; there are CAJUN CROSSINGS here (the holy trinity), and the next bean experiment points the same way.
- CARAWAY BUILD (B): CELERY IS CLASHING.

=== YELLOW/SWEET ONIONS (I THINK) ===

YELLOW or SWEET onions are the onion for this family — they work best, I think.

=== VARIANT A — CHICKPEA + CHARD NOTES ===

SWISS CHARD — STALKS IN THE SOFFRITO, LEAVES TOO (BOTH GOOD): sautéing the stalks in the soffrito works, and the leaves are good too — both. (Walked forward from the earlier stalks-better-than-leaves stance; the stalks still pair beautifully with the chickpeas — same stalks-have-value lesson as the retired chard pickle pasta.)

OREGANO WORKS HERE — UNLIKE ITS NEIGHBORS: oregano works well in this soup (and family-wide across the variants — see the herbs rule) — notable because it doesn't work in similar dishes like [[french-chicken-soup]] or [[chana-masala]].

NO DAIRY; SEASONINGS = OREGANO + BAY LEAF (+ COMPATIBLE: OLD BAY, LEMON ZEST): variant A runs on the stock + tomato + chard + bay leaf + oregano — no dairy. OLD BAY and LEMON ZEST are compatible seasonings here — primary. THYME is family-wide now (walked forward from secondary-in-this-build — see the herbs rule). MUSHROOMS clash, I think — marked clashing; rosemary is out per the family herb rule.

LEMON JUICE — TRIED, SECONDARY: the sourness hunch was right enough to keep — lemon juice is secondary (lemon ZEST is primary).

STANDING CHICKPEA RESCUE: if a chickpea dish reads flat/off, the reliable correction is EXTRA CUMIN + LEMON ZEST — works across cuisines.

=== VARIANT B — CARAWAY CHICKEN NOTES ===

SHREDDED BREAST, NOT THIGH: best with shredded chicken breast as opposed to chicken thigh — the lean shred suits the brothy tomato register where thigh would fatten it.

HERBS — THYME + SAGE (+ OREGANO PER THE FAMILY RULE); ROSEMARY AND CELERY CLASHING: thyme and sage are this build's primary herbs (thyme from the basque spine, sage from the [[french-chicken-soup]] discovery), and oregano is welcome per the family-wide herb rule. Rosemary is clashing family-wide. Celery is clashing in this build (see the celery note).

SOFRITO DISCIPLINE — IMPLICIT BUT REAL: the onions/garlic/tomato are made into a PASTE before deglazing with wine and adding stock for the chicken poach. That's the spanish build order, and it's part of why this build could swing IBERIAN as easily as riviera.

=== WANT TO TRY — ROAST THE TOMATOES AND PEPPERS FIRST (CARAWAY BUILD) ===

Next time: ROAST the tomatoes and peppers before they go in (instead of raw into the sofrito). The [[ottolenghi-cherry-tomatoes]] and retired blender cheat meals variant C roasts point the same direction — roasting concentrates and chars where the sofrito only reduces.

=== WANT TO TRY — THE IBERIAN SWING (CARAWAY BUILD) ===

This could swing IBERIAN or riviera. The levers to try:
- SMOKED PAPRIKA (pimentón) bloomed in the oil — the single biggest spanish signal.
- CHORIZO as the pork (cured, paprika-laden — the pork hypothesis in spanish form; chickpea build + chorizo = garbanzos con chorizo).
- SHERRY VINEGAR in place of the white wine / lemon acid.
- The iberian version would drop the CARAWAY and SAGE and go bay + parsley. (Though note: caraway isn't just central-european — it's sometimes part of HARISSA, which is also mediterranean. The caraway here can be read as the north-african/mediterranean thread, not only the german one.)

=== WANT TO TRY — OTHER PROTEINS: SHRIMP + CHICKEN, OR PORK ALONE (CARAWAY BUILD) ===

I think SHRIMP + CHICKEN could work together (shrimp added late, on top of the chicken), or PORK BY ITSELF (lean shredded — the same lean-over-fatty rule as the breast/thigh call). Shrimp + tomato + peppers + white wine is the basque/provençal coast; pork + caraway (+ the possible pickle experiment) is the german kit crossing over. One tension if shrimp happens: shrimp + caraway is an odd couple — the shrimp version might quietly prefer FENNEL SEED in the caraway slot. Same split for the pickle juice: it would likely HELP chicken or pork in isolation but FIGHT the shrimp if they appear. So the hypotheses cluster into two builds: (1) chicken-or-pork + caraway + pickle, (2) shrimp(+chicken) + fennel, no pickle. Beef judged doubtful — too dark for this spine.

=== WANT TO TRY — PICKLES + PICKLE JUICE (CARAWAY BUILD) ===

Pickles and pickle juice — would be interesting with the jalapeño. (The caraway is already here, so this would be the german tang kit crossing into the southern tomato spine — the caraway + pickle pairing is proven in [[pub-style-lentils]] and the retired chard pickle pasta.)

=== WANT TO TRY — KIDNEY/RED BEANS AS THE MAIN BEAN (CHICKPEA BUILD) ===

Want to try KIDNEY (RED) BEANS as the main bean — part of the cajun-crossings thread in the celery note.

=== WANT TO TRY — BASIL (CHICKPEA BUILD) ===

Want to try BASIL — or see where it connects with the other ingredients here. Probably NOT with the kidney/red beans — but maybe.

=== VARIANT D — THE INSTAPOT SWAP: BARLEY + LENTILS, NOT CHICKPEAS ===

The instapot version swaps the chickpeas for BARLEY + BLACK/GREEN LENTILS (dried) — chickpeas are tough to instapot right. Dried lentils and barley take instapot pressure happily (same logic as [[shittake-lentil-soup]], where the instapot does the lentils and the broth extraction at the same time).

PEPPERS → CARROTS SWAP (THIS BUILD ONLY): I think you could swap out the peppers for carrots if you wanted to — the PEPPERS ARE MORE TIED TO THE CHICKPEAS. With the chickpeas already gone in this build, the core's pepper slot loosens. That swap might turn into a SEPARATE RECIPE eventually (it would leave the chicken stock + raw tomato + bell peppers core behind).

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[chana-masala]] / [[himachali-chana-madra]]: the indian tomato/legume chickpea dishes — different family (curry, not stock soup).
- [[sumac-chickpea-skillet]]: the dry-skillet chickpea format.
- [[minestrone-soup]]: the neighboring italian stock-and-legume soup.
- [[chicken-with-vinegar]]: variant B shares the tomato + chicken stock + thyme rules (and the caraway curiosity) — the source of the basque framing.
- [[french-chicken-soup]]: the other chicken soup — northern register (sage + herbes de provence, dumplings, no tomato).
- chard pickle pasta (retired 2026-11-06): was the other swiss-chard recipe — leaves-forward where variant A is stalks-forward.
why_i_like_this_recipe: Chicken stock + tomato is an unusual combination and it works unreasonably well with chickpeas and swiss chard.
